items.t: Two Brokerages Lift Allianz Targets as Insurer's Fund Arm Drives Record Nine-Month Profit
sum: Allianz shares closed Friday at €476.20, up 1.3%, after a pair of brokerage upgrades rewarded the Munich insurer for a stronger-than-expected third quarter and a brighter full-year outlook. Oddo BHF raised its price target to €490 from €460 while keeping an "Outperform" rating, and DZ Bank lifted its fair value to €508 from €495 with a "Buy" — both moves coming on the heels of the company's quarterly release.

The DZ Bank revision, published Thursday, was framed by analyst Thorsten Wenzel around the group's asset management business, which he said is running well enough to underpin the higher guidance. That upgrade followed Allianz's Wednesday announcement that it now expects full-year operating profit of roughly €18.6 billion, up from a previous ceiling of €18.4 billion. The company attached a caveat: the new range assumes no unforeseen major natural catastrophes or capital market shocks.

For the three months to the end of September 2026, Allianz booked operating profit of €4.7 billion — a 6.2% advance year on year and, according to dpa, about 10% ahead of the analyst consensus. Total business volume in the quarter came in at €44.4 billion, while the adjusted profit attributable to shareholders reached €2.9 billion.
Across the first nine months, operating profit hit a record €14.1 billion, with adjusted period net income attributable to shareholders of €9.3 billion on business volume of €143.0 billion.
Shareholder returns are already running ahead of schedule. Allianz confirmed Thursday that its share buyback programme of up to €2.5 billion had been fully executed back in September 2026.

The combination of a consensus-beating quarter, a nudged-up annual target and a completed repurchase has given the stock fresh momentum into the weekend — and handed the group's fund management division much of the credit for the improved outlook.

sum: Allianz reported a record operating profit for the first nine months of 2026 and raised the upper end of its full-year target. In its earnings release dated Thursday, November 12, the insurer said operating profit for the first nine months rose 7.8 percent year on year to 14.1 billion euros, its highest nine-month level ever.
Allianz stock traded at 474.60 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:13 CET on Friday, November 13, 2026, 0.47 percent above the Xetra close of Thursday, November 12.

Group total business volume reached 143.0 billion euros in the nine-month period, up from 141.2 billion euros a year earlier. Internal growth was 3.8 percent, supported by Asset Management and Property-Casualty insurance.

Asset Management was the main earnings driver. Its nine-month operating profit rose 20.3 percent to 2.9 billion euros, while operating revenues increased 17.8 percent to 7.1 billion euros. Third-party assets under management reached 2.152 trillion euros at September 30, supported by net inflows of 132 billion euros.

Life/Health operating profit increased 3.1 percent to 4.4 billion euros. Property-Casualty operating profit rose 3.2 percent to 7.1 billion euros for the nine months. The combined ratio was 92.2 percent, within Allianz's full-year outlook range of 92 to 93 percent, although the third quarter absorbed a higher natural catastrophe impact.

Shareholders' core net income advanced 10.6 percent to 9.3 billion euros, while core earnings per share climbed 12.7 percent to 24.15 euros. Annualized core return on equity stood at 20.1 percent, and the Solvency II capitalization ratio was 219 percent at the end of September.

For the third quarter alone, operating profit rose 6.2 percent to 4.7 billion euros. Allianz attributed the increase to a strong Asset Management result, higher business volume and margins, and a solid contribution from Life/Health. The company also said high capital market volatility and elevated natural catastrophe losses affected the period.

sum: Allianz reported a record operating profit of 14.1 billion euros for the first nine months of 2026 and raised the upper end of its full-year outlook. The company published the third-quarter and nine-month results on Thursday, November 12, according to its Allianz earnings release.

Third-quarter total business volume reached 44.4 billion euros, with internal growth of 3.0 percent. Operating profit increased 6.2 percent to 4.7 billion euros, supported by Asset Management and Life/Health. Shareholders' core net income rose 1.2 percent to 2.9 billion euros.

Allianz said Property-Casualty remained resilient despite a higher impact from natural catastrophes. The insurer also pointed to high capital-market volatility, while describing the contribution from its diversified business model as broad-based.

For the first nine months, total business volume stood at 143.0 billion euros, representing internal growth of 3.8 percent from the prior year. Operating profit rose 7.8 percent from 13.1 billion euros to 14.1 billion euros, the highest nine-month level in Allianz's history. Asset Management was the main growth driver, while all business segments were ahead of their pro-rata full-year operating-profit outlooks.

Shareholders' core net income advanced 10.6 percent to 9.3 billion euros. Core earnings per share increased 12.7 percent to 24.15 euros, while annualized core return on equity reached 20.1 percent. The Solvency II ratio was 219 percent, one percentage point above the level at the end of 2025.

Following the performance, Allianz lifted the upper end of its 2026 operating-profit target range to 18.6 billion euros. The original range was 17.4 billion euros plus or minus 1 billion euros, subject to significant natural catastrophes and capital-market events.

Allianz stock traded at 469.15 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:18:56 CET on Thursday, November 12, 2026, 1.20 percent above the Xetra close of Wednesday, November 11, at 463.60 euros. The quote places the shares above the previous Xetra session's close as investors assess the record result and higher target.

Allianz Faces a Double Reckoning: Climate Reality in 2064, Earnings Reality on November 12
sum: Allianz has handed investors two very different documents to digest within the space of a week. One is a sustainability report that projects global carbon neutrality, at current pace, will not arrive until 2064. The other is a pair of analyst notes that keep the stock firmly in buy territory — with price targets that sit a long way above where the shares actually trade.

Start with the climate math. The insurer published its "Green Transition Tracker 2026" on November 5, and its verdict on the world's net-zero journey is blunt: the transition remains well behind target. Buried in the same report, however, is a genuine milestone — renewables overtook coal in 2025 to become the largest source of global electricity generation. Allianz presents that shift alongside its broader warning that the pace of decarbonisation is still too slow.

The equity story is running on a faster clock. Metzler Capital Markets lifted its price target on the stock from €454 to €490 on Friday and reiterated its buy rating, according to media reports. The reasoning rests on the profit outlook for 2026 and on momentum in the non-life insurance business. Berenberg, for its part, reaffirmed its own buy recommendation and a €684 target on Monday, once again naming Allianz its preferred pick among European composite insurers ahead of AXA. Berenberg's case leans on the same two pillars: a strong 2026 earnings outlook and the vigour of non-life.

That both houses have converged on identical drivers is telling. It also sets a clear test. The bull case now stands or falls on whether Allianz can demonstrate, in hard numbers, that non-life momentum is durable rather than a passing tailwind. Investors who anchor their valuation to continued operating strength will want the company's own commentary to carry the same confidence as its backward-looking results.

The gap between the two targets — €490 versus €684 — is worth pausing on. Similar arguments, markedly different conclusions. That spread argues for weighing the business assumptions behind each number rather than the headline figure itself.
The shares have already travelled some distance. Allianz is up 19% since the start of the year, and closed yesterday at €465.30, a gain of 1.7% on the day.

sum: Sanlam Allianz Holdings (Kenya) faces a mandated shareholder sell-down after Kenya's Insurance Regulatory Authority approved deferred shares from the insurer's 2025 rights issue. Business Daily reported the development on Wednesday, November 4, 2026.

The approval dated September 28, 2026, covers 100.58 million shares that had been held back after the rights issue. It raises Sanlam Allianz Africa's direct and indirect holding to 71.47 percent from 66.19 percent, above the ownership threshold for Kenyan insurers.

Sanlam Allianz Africa plans to dispose of at least 30,946,202 ordinary shares, equivalent to 4.81 percent of the enlarged share capital, by September 28, 2027. The buyers must meet East African Community eligibility requirements. The sale method, buyer and transaction price have not been announced.

The deferred shares arose from a 2025 rights issue that offered 500 million shares at KES 5.00 each to raise KES 2.5 billion, mainly for debt repayment. The allotment dilutes the holdings of other investors and increases the listed company's issued share capital from 543.42 million to 644 million shares.

Sanlam Allianz Holdings (Kenya) is a Nairobi-listed insurance group serving the Kenyan market. Its life insurance business is held through the listed structure, while its general insurance business operates in an unlisted affiliate following the earlier restructuring. The group's broader profile also includes insurance and financial-services activities in East Africa.

Allianz Looks Past a One-Day Slide Toward a November 12 Earnings Reckoning
sum: Allianz shares shed 2.7% on Friday, caught in a downdraft that swept across European insurance stocks and left the Munich-based group among the session's laggards. The wider sector retreated 2.6%, according to Reuters, as investors digested downgrades of reinsurers Munich Re and Hannover Rück by JPMorgan alongside a broader flight from risk tied to worries about AI-related equities.

The pullback put a temporary dent in what has otherwise been a constructive backdrop for the stock. Metzler lifted its price target on Allianz to EUR 490 from EUR 454 while reaffirming its buy recommendation, a vote of confidence that stood in contrast to the day's trading mood.

Attention now shifts to November 12, when Allianz will publish its third-quarter 2026 results. The release is scheduled for 7 a.m., and it represents the next company-specific catalyst capable of moving the shares independently of sector sentiment.

That distinction matters. Friday's decline was driven by forces largely outside Allianz's control — reinsurance downgrades and a general retreat from risk assets — rather than by any change in the company's own prospects. The quarterly report offers investors a chance to weigh the business on its own merits.

The stakes cut both ways. Should Allianz deliver convincing figures and the pressure on insurers ease, the two forces could reinforce each other, giving any recovery a firmer footing than a purely sentiment-driven rebound. A disappointing print against a still-fragile sector backdrop would compound the pressure, layering company-specific doubts on top of industry-wide weakness.
Separately on Friday, Allianz issued a mandatory notification on its total voting rights, putting the new figure at roughly 374 million. The disclosure concerns the voting rights of Allianz SE.

On the strategic front, Allianz Commercial confirmed plans announced Thursday to establish a new direct insurance syndicate at Lloyd's, to be named "Allianz Commercial 1893." Operations are slated to begin on January 1, 2027, subject to final regulatory approval — a caveat the company built explicitly into its timetable.

Allianz Faces Twin Headwinds as Reinsurance Gloom Meets a Metzler Vote of Confidence
sum: Allianz shares came under pressure on two fronts, shedding 2.7% in Friday trading as a broad flight from European insurance names collided with a JPMorgan downgrade of the German reinsurance sector. The wider European insurance index fell 2.6%, with Munich Re caught in the same downdraft.

The sell-off unfolded against a turbulent market backdrop. Reuters reported a stampede out of AI and semiconductor stocks across US and Asian exchanges, compounded by worries over tighter artificial-intelligence regulation following the US midterm elections. Allianz numbered among the DAX constituents in sharp decline, and rising US Treasury yields — triggered by stronger-than-expected American payroll data — added further weight to the market's mood.

JPMorgan's downgrade of Hannover Rück and Munich Re centered on expectations of continued softening in reinsurance pricing. The broker anticipates further double-digit rate declines at the January 2027 contract renewals. The trend is already visible: natural catastrophe coverage was priced roughly 12% cheaper at the January renewals, and by mid-year the reduction had widened to about 15%. That trajectory puts earnings quality across the insurance business under scrutiny, and Allianz stock lost 2.9% in today's session as selling pressure persisted.

Against the sector's skeptical turn, Metzler has staked out a more constructive position. The research house expects Allianz to lift its operating profit guidance to the upper half of its target range when it reports results. The current 2026 target stands at EUR 17.4 billion, with a tolerance band of one billion euros either side.

Confirmation of that upgrade would signal stronger underlying momentum — but until Allianz delivers, the optimism remains contingent on the upcoming release. Third-quarter figures are due on 12 November 2026, with the media call scheduled for 09:30 and the analyst conference following at 14:30.

The company brings a growing earnings base into that report. First-half 2026 operating profit rose 8.6%, while adjusted net income reached EUR 6.4 billion. Whether that growth translates into a stronger valuation hinges on claims development: rising profits count in the company's favor only so long as a heavier claims burden does not erode the operational improvement.

Maybank IB allotted 225mil shares in Big Caring IPO for price stabilisation measures
sum: KUALA LUMPUR: Maybank Investment Bank has announced that it has been granted an over-allotment option comprising up to 225.15 million shares for the upcoming initial public offering (IPO) of Big Caring Group Bhd (BCG).

In a Bursa Malaysia filing by BCG, Maybank IB stated that BCG's shares may be subject to stabilising action following the IPO. The option is designated strictly for the purpose of covering any over-allotments of shares during the IPO.
The maximum threshold represents exactly 12.0 per cent of the total number of shares offered under the IPO.

The stabilisation period will officially commence on Nov 19, the listing date of BCG on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia. According to the announcement, Maybank IB's mandate to stabilise the share price will remain active until the earlier of two specific milestones:
The date falling 30 days from, and including, the official listing date; or
The date when the stabilising manager has successfully purchased the full aggregate limit of 225.15 million shares on the open market.
The mechanism is designed to prevent or slow a decline in the market price of the shares following their debut, providing early market stability for incoming investors.

Allianz Redraws Its Distribution Map Ahead of November 12 Earnings Test
sum: Allianz has spent the final days of October strengthening the routes through which it reaches customers, pairing a renewed travel-insurance alliance with a fresh foothold in German car finance. The two moves land just over a fortnight before the group publishes third-quarter 2026 results on November 12 — the next hard checkpoint for judging whether broader distribution is translating into earnings.

The travel side rests on continuity. Allianz Partners and the TUI Group extended their strategic cooperation by a further four years on October 28, covering eleven European markets. The renewal took effect on Sunday, and the next phase is slated to focus on AI-supported travel insurance products alongside additional markets and sales channels. That forward-looking language describes priorities rather than an expansion already completed, leaving open whether the plans will generate incremental business.

Where TUI represents an extension, the group's motor-cover arrangement is a switch in Allianz's favour. On October 27, Allianz Versicherungs-AG became insurance partner to Mercedes-Benz Bank in Germany with immediate effect, Reuters reported, displacing the Talanx subsidiary HDI. Liability and comprehensive policies are now marketed through Mercedes-Benz dealerships at the point of vehicle purchase, embedding cover directly in the buying process.

The two announcements share a common logic even though they differ in structure: insurance is attached to the moment a customer needs protection — booking a trip, driving off a forecourt — rather than sold only through a standalone policy. One continues an existing travel partnership; the other hands Allianz a new distribution channel in its home market.

Behind the distribution news, two executives have taken up new posts. Laurent Floquet has moved to the helm of Allianz Direct, succeeding Kroetz, who transferred from the top of Allianz Direct to Allianz Partners. The reshuffle alone offers no yardstick for future earnings — the business figures will settle that.

Analysts, meanwhile, are reading the same company very differently. Michael Huttner pointed to the strong performance of Pimco and robust earnings in the life insurance business, a view that leans on the earning power of Allianz's existing franchises.

Asia shares bend under AI stress; Apple earnings loom
sum: SYDNEY: Asian share markets slipped on Monday as worries about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence (AI) investment boom loomed over the tech sector, while the high price of oil limited the safe-haven appeal of sovereign bonds.

Concerns about negative cash flow and the sheer scale of AI capex saw the cost of insuring against corporate defaults blow out last week, while gold hit a one-year low amid talk stressed investors were selling to raise money for margin calls.
An added wrinkle is the midterm elections in the United States, where a win by Democrats in either or both houses could result in more political hurdles for data centres.
Adding to the air of unease were withdrawals from Binance as the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange went back online on Sunday after hackers stole billions from the platform last week.
All of which raises the stakes for earnings this week with Apple, AMD and Palantir set to report in the wake of Intel's near 29 per cent tumble on Friday.

Analysts at Goldman Sachs expect capex by hyperscalers to almost double to US$800 billion this year, and rise further to US$1.2 trillion in 2027. At the same time, they see S&P 500 earnings per share growth of nearly 30 per cent in 2026, slowing to 18 per cent next year.

"Earnings results have underscored the fundamental challenge facing equity investors - earnings growth is strong, but it is no longer accelerating," wrote Ben Snider, Goldman's chief US equity strategist, in a note.

Allianz's Singapore Gambit Puts a 28-Billion-Euro Prize Within Reach as Shares Circle Record Territo
sum: The insurance giant's Asian expansion strategy is gathering momentum at a pace that has caught the attention of even seasoned market observers. Allianz Global Investors, the asset management arm of the Munich-based insurer, has confirmed the acquisition of UOB Asset Management from Singapore's United Overseas Bank in a deal valued at 555 million Singapore dollars, equivalent to approximately 376 million euros.

The transaction, announced on Wednesday, represents the second major acquisition in Asia within days — a clear signal that CEO Oliver Bäte's stated priority of growth in the region is translating into action. For AllianzGI, the purchase brings roughly 28 billion euros in assets under management, spanning operations in Singapore and seven additional markets including Brunei, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam.

The acquisition extends well beyond a straightforward asset purchase. AllianzGI gains access to UOB's customer network, and the two parties have agreed to a long-term distribution partnership that will allow them to jointly market investment products to more than 8 million clients across the region. The roughly 500 employees of UOB Asset Management will transfer to AllianzGI, with their positions preserved.

For the seller, the transaction carries its own financial logic. UOB anticipates a pre-tax gain of approximately 330 million Singapore dollars from the sale, which the bank frames as part of its strategic focus. The deal is expected to close in 2027, subject to customary regulatory approvals.

Once the acquisition is complete, AllianzGI's Asian assets under management will reach 170 billion euros. In Singapore specifically, the Allianz subsidiary stands to double its business. AllianzGI chief Tobias Pross described UOB Asset Management as "one of Southeast Asia's leading asset managers, with highly regarded investment capabilities and a strong distribution network" — language that underscores the strategic importance of the purchase.
The equity market has taken the news in stride. Allianz shares were trading at 437.70 euros, just shy of the 52-week high of 438.50 euros reached on the same day.

Turkey’s top 5 insurance companies dominate non-life market in 2026
sum: International Correspondent: Turkey’s insurance sector maintains steady growth, led by non-life insurers amid economic recovery, rising motor and health demand, and digital transformation.

1. Turkiye Sigorta remains the clear market leader with 14-16% share in non-life insurance. The state-backed company recorded 147 billion TRY in premiums in 2025, up 45% year-on-year. It excels in motor, health, and property coverage with extensive reach via PTT branches and a mobile app boasting millions of users.

2. Allianz Sigorta holds second place with 11-13% market share. The international player generated strong premiums through diversified products in auto, health, and life, supported by advanced digital claims processing and high customer satisfaction.

3. Anadolu Anonim Türk Sigorta (Anadolu Sigorta) secures third position with around 9% share. Backed by İşbank, it offers reliable motor and general insurance products with a large domestic customer base and consistent performance.

4. AXA Sigorta ranks fourth with approximately 7-9% market share. Known for international expertise, it provides competitive health, property, and commercial insurance alongside efficient service and strong solvency.
5. HDI Sigorta (or Sompo Sigorta) rounds out the top five with growing 5-7% share. Both focus on non-life segments including commercial lines, delivering competitive offerings amid sector expansion.
These companies benefit from Turkey’s low insurance penetration and ongoing digital adoption. Analysts project further growth in 2026 driven by regulatory support and economic stabilization.

Antique begins Buy call on Canara HSBC Life shares
sum: Antique Stock Broking has initiated coverage of Canara HSBC Life Insurance Co. Ltd., assigning a “Buy” recommendation and outlining its view on the insurer’s risk-return profile as the company lifts its protection business and maintains bancassurance-led growth in India. The initiation follows Canara HSBC Life’s first year as a listed company on the BSE and NSE. Antique has set a target price of ₹190 per share, indicating potential upside of about 26.7% from the previous close. The brokerage’s estimates place the stock at 1.7 times and 1.5 times its projected price-to-embedded value for fiscal years 2027 and 2028, respectively.

In its initiation report cited by Business Standard, Antique said Canara HSBC Life recorded an individual weighted premium income (WPI) compound annual growth rate of about 21% over fiscal 2015-25, with growth of roughly 20% in year-to-date fiscal 2026. Over the same period, Indian life insurance industry growth on this metric was around 10% to 11%, according to the brokerage. The company’s individual WPI market share increased from 1.6% in fiscal 2015 to 2.9% in year-to-date fiscal 2026. Recently disclosed results for the nine months ended Dec. 31, 2025, are consistent with that trend. Individual WPI reached ₹1,915.3 crore, up 20.5% year on year. Total annualized premium equivalent (APE) was ₹2,095 crore, a 22.3% rise from ₹1,713.3 crore a year earlier.

New business premium from individual and group lines grew 28.1% year on year to ₹2,929.4 crore, and renewal premium rose 34.4% to ₹4,001.9 crore. Total premium income for the period was ₹6,931.4 crore, an increase of 31.6%. Assets under management stood at ₹46,888.7 crore, up 17.2% from the prior-year period. Profit after tax was ₹91.9 crore for the nine months, 8.2% higher than a year earlier. On an APE basis, the product mix comprised unit-linked products at 61%, annuities at 12%, non-participating savings at 13%, non-participating protection at 7%, and participating products at 5%. Persistency ratios were reported at 85.6% for the 13th month and 59.2% for the 61st month.
